request.spec:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've made the change, and all 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

The only file changed is `src/main/frontend/features/consolidated/consolidated.slot.tsx`. I didn't need to touch the stored data or the server.

- **Due-total and overdue-total:** each sheet now passes up every person's own figure instead of its already-trimmed total. The consolidated view puts all of them together, skips `n/a`, and leaves out the single highest and single lowest over the whole tree when three or more people have a figure.
- **People count:** each sheet now passes up every person's name and aliases, compared ignoring case, the way the server already matches names. People who share any name or alias count as one person. That carries through chains, so if A matches B and B matches C, all three count once.
- **Same person on two sheets:** their figures are still trimmed separately, not added together first. The first test needs this: it expects 9.00, and merging Ada's two figures would give 7.00.

The per-grade due-totals and the status counts work as before.
